deep.reconstruction:
This page has no computations. It is a heavily corrected prose draft, with many deletions and interlinear insertions, of the introductory part of Riemann's 1857 self-announcement (Selbstanzeige, Göttinger gelehrte Anzeigen/Nachrichten). The announcement is for his memoir 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen'. The next page is a draft of the memoir's own introduction (Gauss series, Kummer in Crelle 15, branches P', P'', linear substitutions under circuits).

Content of the draft, in order:

(1) Purpose. 'In the following memoir I have treated this transcendent [the hypergeometric function] by a new method, which essentially remains applicable to every function satisfying a linear differential equation with algebraic coefficients.' In modern terms, every solution of y^(n) + a_1(z) y^(n-1) + ... + a_n(z) y = 0 with a_i algebraic in z.
- The method allows the previously known results, partly found laboriously ('mühsam', 'schwerfällig, umständlich' are deleted variants), to be perceived ('wahrnehmen').
- The deleted alternative was to base everything on a series Σ valid for all complex values.
- The aim is a convenient overview of the function's possible representations, chiefly for applications in astronomical and physical investigations.

(2) Geometric representation. The value of the independent variable z = x + yi is represented by a point of an infinite plane with rectangular coordinates x, y. Every function of x, y is then a quantity depending on position in the plane.

(3) Analytic functions and continuation. An expression depending on x, y only through x + yi satisfies dw/dx = dw/(i dy) (the Cauchy–Riemann equation in complex form, ∂w/∂y = i ∂w/∂x).
- A function given on a part of the plane, e.g. by a convergent series Σ, that satisfies this equation can be continued continuously in a manner fixed by the equation. This is analytic continuation.
- Riemann adds that the continuation may not proceed through mere lines. A differential equation cannot be applied along a line, so the continuation must go through surface pieces of finite width.

(4) Multivaluedness. Depending on the path, the continuations can take different values for the same value of the variable. There are certain points of the plane around which the function continues into another one. Example: the point a for log(z−a).
- (My gloss: one circuit around a adds 2πi.)

(5) Terminology.
- 'For easier understanding of the multivaluedness', the different continuations of a function over the same part of the plane are to be called branches (Zweige) of the function.
- A value around which one branch continues into another is called a branch value (Verzweigungswerth) of the function.
- A value at which no branching occurs: the function is called (reading uncertain) 'einändrig'/single-valued there.
- The last, garbled line says that all branches satisfy the same differential equation. This leads into the next page: any three branches are linearly dependent, and circuits act by linear substitutions with constant coefficients.

The draft largely matches, sometimes verbatim, the published text of the 1857 Anzeige. Examples: 'nach einer neuen Methode behandelt, welche im Wesentlichen auf jede Function, die einer linearen Differentialgleichung mit algebraischen Coefficienten genügt, anwendbar bleibt'; 'astronomischen und physikalischen Untersuchungen'; 'Zweige', 'Verzweigungswerth', and log(z−a) as the example.
errors: No mathematical errors. The only formula, dw/dx = dw/(i dy), is the correct complex form of the Cauchy–Riemann equations for w = f(x+iy).

The remark that continuation cannot run along mere lines but needs strips of finite width is heuristic: a differential equation cannot be applied on a line. It is correct in spirit; modern continuation uses chains of overlapping discs.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the published 1857 self-announcement of Riemann's hypergeometric memoir; many phrases match the printed text. It gives some insight into how Riemann composed the text, e.g. the deleted plan to base things on a series Σ valid for all complex values, but no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: A function of x+iy satisfies dw/dx = dw/(i dy) (Cauchy–Riemann in complex form)
One positive circuit around the branch value a changes log(z−a) by 2πi, so a is a branch point
A function of x, y not depending only on x+iy fails the equation dw/dx = dw/(i dy)

transcription_corrections: The page is a draft of the 1857 Anzeige (self-announcement) of the hypergeometric memoir. Reconstructed passages from the printed text: 'Zur leichtern Auffassung ... denke man sich den Werth der unabhängig veränderlichen Grösse z = x+yi vertreten durch einen Punkt einer unendlichen Ebene, dessen rechtwinklige Coordinaten x, y sind'.
'welcher' after 'neuen Methode behandelt' should read 'welche ... anwendbar bleibt' (published wording).
'dw/dy i' should be read as dw/(i dy), i.e. ∂w/∂x = (1/i) ∂w/∂y.
'gelindesten [?]' is uncertain; context suggests 'Umlaufen/umgehen' of a point by lines. Reading unclear.
'einändrig [?]' is uncertain. It may be 'einwerthig' or a similar term for single-valued/unbranched at that value.
'für denselben Werth von x' should be read in context as values of the complex variable (Riemann alternates z and x for the variable).
